        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. It is normalized before being stored and
            returned: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and internal runs of whitespace
            collapsed to a single space, the value is upper-cased and common abbreviations are
            expanded as whole tokens (ST -> STREET, RD -> ROAD, AVE -> AVENUE). So

            dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must contain 8 to 15 digits after

            tolerates an optional leading '+' plus digits and separators (spaces, brackets,
            dashes); numbers that cannot form valid E.164 are rejected with 400.

I implemented the `membershipNumber` field formatted as `<customerCode>-M<YY>`, where `YY` is the last two digits of the owner's `registrationDate` year.

Since the value is derived entirely from the owner's own fields (`customerCode` + `registrationDate`), I computed it at read time in the mapper — matching the existing pattern used for the other read-only derived fields (`displayName`, `initials`) rather than persisting a redundant column.

**Changes:**

It returns `null` when either source field is absent (consistent with the spec and null-safety of the sibling formatters). The `%02d` guarantees the two-digit, zero-padded year (e.g. `SMI-0007-M26`).

The acceptance test `coreMembershipNumberFormat`, which reads the owner back and asserts `customerCode + "-M" + YY == membershipNumber`, passes.
